articles.headline: Sources: Colts' Pierce out weeks; hoping for return midseason
articles.description: Colts WR Alec Pierce is expected to miss several weeks with a heel injury but will attempt to avoid surgery in the hopes of returning midseason.
articles.headlineJa: 情報筋：コルツのピアースが数週間離脱へ、シーズン中盤の復帰を目指す
articles.descriptionJa: コルツのWRアレク・ピアースはかかとの負傷で数週間離脱する見込みですが、シーズン中盤での復帰を目指し手術を回避する方針です。
articles.body:
Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Alec Pierce is expected to miss several weeks after aggravating a left heel injury in Sunday night's loss to the Kansas City Chiefs, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

Pierce will attempt to rehab the injury rather than have surgery, sources said, with the hope that he could return midseason. Surgery is still on the table depending how the rehab goes. It's likely the wideout will be placed on injured reserve while he recovers.

The injury is to the same heel that Pierce had surgically repaired in March. His recovery from that procedure stretched longer than expected, with him missing training camp and returning to practice only last month. 

Pierce, who signed a four-year, $114 million contract in March, was expected to be a centerpiece of the Colts' offense this season. 

The Colts, already thin at receiver because of veteran backup Ashton Dulin 's ankle injury, moved swiftly to address the position by agreeing to terms Monday evening with free agent Darius Slayton, sources told ESPN. A fellow member of the New York Giants ' 2019 draft class alongside current Colts quarterback Daniel Jones, Slayton caught 37 passes for 538 yards last season with the Giants. Slayton started 12 games last season.

The Colts' offense struggled to create explosive plays on Sunday following Pierce's injury. But Slayton, even at 29, is seen as a player who can potentially stretch the field. He has averaged a healthy 15 yards-per-catch in his career, including 14.5 last season. Jones has so far had difficulty replicating the explosiveness seen in the Colts' offense last season, when he averaged 8.1 yards per attempt. Through two games -- with Pierce limited in Week 1 and missing most of Sunday's game after his injury -- Jones has averaged 6.1 yards per attempt.

Slayton had his best seasons while playing alongside Jones in New York. In the four seasons he's played with Jones, at least in part, Slayton has surpassed 700 receiving yards.

ESPN's Stephen Holder contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Giants QB Jaxson Dart exits MNF game vs. Rams with knee injury
articles.description: Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart is questionable to return to Monday night's game against the Rams after taking a hard hit on his left knee in the first quarter.
articles.body:
INGLEWOOD, Calif. -- New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart left Monday night's game against the Los Angeles Rams after taking a hard hit on his left knee on his team's opening series.

Dart went to the blue tent, where he was examined by medical personnel. He came out and walked with a limp to the locker room.

The team said he was questionable to return due to a knee injury. 

Dart was hurt while being pressured on third-and-8. Rams linebacker Byron Young hit Dart from the quarterback's right side, sending him into linebacker Josaiah Stewart, who undercut Dart's legs and sent him down hard onto the turf. 

The second-year quarterback immediately went to the ground and grabbed at his left knee. He had completed 3 of 5 passes for 20 yards.

Dart wasn't the only Giants star who left the game in the first half. Wide receiver Malik Nabers was hurt trying to make a catch in the second quarter.

Cornerback Trent McDuffie knocked down a pass intended for Nabers, who immediately grabbed at his right shoulder. Nabers went to the sideline and sank to the ground, where he was attended to by trainers for several minutes.

The third-year wide receiver, who came back last week from a torn ACL, then went to the bench and put a towel over his head. He was initially listed as questionable but did return to the field later in the quarter. 

Jameis Winston replaced Dart at quarterback. 

Winston started two games and appeared in three for the Giants in 2025, throwing for 567 yards with two touchdowns and two interceptions. The 11-year veteran was drafted No. 1 in 2015 and has also played for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, New Orleans Saints and Cleveland Browns.

Information from The Associated Press was included in this report.

articles.headline: River Ryan makes strong debut and Tigers hit 3 home runs in 9-2 win over Nationals
articles.description: — River Ryan was outstanding in his Detroit debut and the Tigers hit three home runs to rout the Washington Nationals 9-2 on Monday night, one day after being eliminated from the American League playoff race.
articles.body:
DETROIT -- — River Ryan was outstanding in his Detroit debut and the Tigers hit three home runs to rout the Washington Nationals 9-2 on Monday night, one day after being eliminated from the American League playoff race.


              Ryan, acquired from the Los Angeles Dodgers in the Tarik Skubal trade, pitched three scoreless innings. He allowed two hits and a walk with two strikeouts. Ryan is expected to start again in the season finale Sunday — the day after Justin Verlander is scheduled to make his final major league start.


              Keider Montero (10-9) pitched four scoreless innings in relief of Ryan.


              Washington starter DJ Herz (0-1) made his first big league appearance in nearly two years. Herz, who had Tommy John surgery in April 2025, pitched four innings, allowing four runs on five hits and two walks while striking out four.


              The Tigers took a 2-0 lead in the first. Gleyber Torres walked, went to second on a wild pitch and scored on a ground-rule double from Hao-Yu Lee. After Herz got the first out, Eduardo Valencia singled to left field, with Lee scoring when James Wood misplayed the ball for an error.


              Javier Báez made it 4-0 in the fourth, hitting his third homer of the season over the Tigers bullpen in left to bring home Dillon Dingler.


              Detroit added five more runs in the fifth, three on Ben Malgeri's fourth homer and two on Spencer Torkelson's 25th.


              That made it 9-0, but Yohandy Morales hit a two-run homer to get the Nationals on the scoreboard in the eighth.


              The Tigers announced before the game that, due to a bank merger, Comerica Park will be known as Fifth Third Park starting in 2027. That's the same name as the stadium for the Toledo Mud Hens, Detroit's Triple-A team.


              Up next
              The teams continue their three-game series Tuesday, with Detroit RHP Drew Anderson (5-6, 3.62 ERA) facing LHP Jackson Kent (1-4, 6.40).


              ------

articles.headline: Jays' Dylan Cease avoids serious injury, won't need surgery
articles.description: The MRI on Toronto Blue Jays pitcher Dylan Cease's right shoulder showed only inflammation and not anything more serious, he told reporters Monday.
articles.body:
The MRI on Toronto Blue Jays pitcher Dylan Cease's right shoulder showed only inflammation and not anything more serious that would require surgery, he told reporters Monday. 

Cease, 30, underwent the MRI after he was scratched from his upcoming start Wednesday. Toronto manager John Schneider told reporters Sunday that Cease has been dealing with a shoulder issue for the past few weeks that includes a decrease in velocity.

"The velocity being down has been a little bit concerning." Cease said, according to MLB.com. "But at the same time, I'm getting outs. It wasn't anything that was too scary because nothing about it feels like I've got something that needs surgery. I was never that panicked or worried, it was more of an inconvenience, and I was annoyed that I wasn't able to maximize my best self.

"The last couple of starts, the velo keeps going down and down. Especially that last one, I almost felt like I was hurting the team."

Cease might still be unlikely to pitch again this season for a Blue Jays team that has a slim chance to earn a wild-card playoff berth. But the results mean Toronto shouldn't expect any delay in getting back its ace pitcher for 2027. Cease is in the first year of a seven-year, $210 million deal he signed with Toronto last winter. 

Cease has had a stellar season, posting a 2.40 ERA while leading the American League in strikeouts per nine innings at 12.7. He accumulated 5.5 fWAR, good for second in the AL behind only Cam Schlittler of the New York Yankees.

The Blue Jays are also dealing with injuries to star slugger Vladimir Guerrero Jr. and now rookie outfielder Brett Bateman, who was hurt making a sliding catch in the second inning of Monday's game against the Baltimore Orioles.

Bateman held onto the ball to retire Baltimore's Rece Hinds, but his slide left a divot in the turf and he rolled over awkwardly after making the catch. Bateman was able to walk off the field, but very slowly, and he was replaced the next time Toronto was in the field.

Precautionary X-rays for Bateman were negative for a fracture, according to the team. 

The Blue Jays entered the day three games behind the Chicago White Sox for the final wild card in the American League. Guerrero was out of the lineup because of back trouble. Starting pitcher Trey Yesavage was limited to two innings in his first game back from knee inflammation.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Giants put Eldridge on concussion list after accident at hotel
articles.description: Bryce Eldridge's strong rookie season for San Francisco appears to have come to an end.
articles.headlineJa: ジャイアンツ、ホテルでの事故後にエルドリッジを脳震盪リストへ登録
articles.descriptionJa: サンフランシスコ・ジャイアンツのブライス・エルドリッジの好調なルーキーシーズンは、どうやら終了を迎えたようです。
articles.body:
SAN FRANCISCO -- Bryce Eldridge's strong rookie season for the San Francisco Giants appears to have ended after the Giants put the first baseman/designated hitter on the seven-day concussion list Monday.

The move is retroactive to Sept. 18, which means Eldridge could play in the Giants' final three games against the Los Angeles Dodgers this weekend. But San Francisco manager Tony Vitello said he doesn't anticipate Eldridge playing again in 2026.

Eldridge, 21, sustained a head injury in an accident at the team hotel in Los Angeles on Friday. He is hitting .269 with 17 home runs and 57 RBIs in 386 at-bats. He made his season debut May 4.

The Giants drafted Eldridge in the first round (No. 16) in 2023 out of James Madison High in Vienna, Virginia. Eldridge had not played first base until 2024, his second pro season.

Vitello said Eldridge's improved defensive work was perhaps the most impressive part of his rookie year.

"The easy way to look at him is, 'All right, we called him up. Let's see some home runs,'" Vitello said. "And he hit more than his fair share, and some of them were pretty dramatic and important -- but he did a lot of other little, small things."

The Giants made other roster moves Monday. They put outfielder Jung Hoo Lee (.276, 10 HRs) on the 10-day injured list because of a groin contusion. San Francisco reinstated infielder Marcelo Mayer from the 10-day injured list and selected outfielder Bo Davidson from Triple-A Sacramento.

Mayer came to the Giants in a trade deadline deal with Boston last month in which the Red Sox acquired left-handed reliever Erik Miller. Mayer was set to make his Giants debut as the designated hitter in their game against Minnesota on Monday night.

Davidson also was in the lineup as the right fielder against the Twins. Considered one of the Giants' top prospects, Davidson will be making his big league debut. Between Double-A and Triple-A this season, the left-handed batter hit .290 with 29 homers, 94 RBIs and 20 stolen bases.

In another roster move, the Giants designated left-handed reliever Philip Abner for assignment.

articles.headline: Rams WR Puka Nacua (hip) inactive for MNF vs. Giants
articles.description: Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua was inactive for Monday night's game against the New York Giants.
articles.headlineJa: ラムズWRプカ・ナクア（股関節）がジャイアンツとのMNFで不活性（欠場）に
articles.descriptionJa: ロサンゼルス・ラムズのワイドレシーバー、プカ・ナクアは月曜夜のニューヨーク・ジャイアンツ戦に出場しません。
articles.body:
INGLEWOOD, Calif. -- Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua was inactive for Monday night's game against the New York Giants.

Nacua was added to the Rams' injury report Friday because of a hip injury. On Saturday, McVay said Nacua was dealing with "a little bit of soreness" in his groin and would not practice that day.

McVay said the Rams were "being smart" with Nacua because he is a skill player. The coach also said Nacua's injury wasn't related to the psoas injury that caused him to miss time during training camp.

McVay said that day that though Nacua practiced Thursday, he "didn't feel totally like himself [with] his ability to be able to kind of open up and really hit full speed."

In the Rams' season opener, Nacua led the Rams with five catches for 74 yards on nine targets.

Rams wide receiver Jordan Whittington, who was added to the injury report Friday because of a quad injury, was also inactive.

articles.headline: NFL Week 2's best arrivals, led by Aaron Donald and Jaxson Dart
articles.description: Rounding up the top pregame and tunnel arrivals from around the league.
articles.headlineJa: アーロン・ドナルドとジャクソン・ダートを筆頭とするNFL第2週のベスト私服・スタジアム入りファッション
articles.descriptionJa: リーグ全体の試合前やトンネル（入場口）での注目ファッションをまとめました。
articles.body:
There are no rules for the best NFL gameday arrival fits, but there is certainly an unspoken competition, and the judges are often a player's football peers.

An animated discussion among Cincinnati Bengals defenders in the locker room after a win illustrated this.

The source was cornerback DJ Turner II's custom bold double-breasted suit by fashion designer Pharoah Kirk -- the unofficial fit of the day. Respect was given to Turner's fit, with one player promising to top his arrival the following week.

"I'm always about that action," Turner said. I gotta put it on."

Week 1 started with a bang, as many players put on their Sunday best to open the season, but just like on the field, consistency is king. This Sunday could provide much stiffer competition.

Here are some of the most interesting NFL arrivals from Week 2.

Monday night fits

Playing in his first game in over 900 days, Los Angeles Rams star Aaron Donald wore a simple black jacket and shorts with black-rimmed glasses. The player he'll be looking to bring down, New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart, rocked a bomber jacket from the brand Nahmias and camouflage pants.

The Giants made the most of the "Monday Night Football" stage.

Backup quarterback Jameis Winston angora sleeveless shirt was the highlight of this all-cream fit. Linebacker Brian Burns' Loewe's blue pinstripe jacket was strong -- a sophisticated energy from one of NFL's best pass rushers. Right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor's lime green splatter jacket with beige pants from Gentleman's Playbook was unique and bold. A big man going shirtless under a jacket is a different level of confidence.

Here are the tops looks from "Monday Night Football."

Sunday night drip

Indianapolis Colts defensive lineman DeForest Buckner might have had the best outfit ahead of Sunday's matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs. Buckner wore a navy and black silk suit made by Gentleman's Playbook. It was a bold and unique choice.

Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce also showed up in style with a Louis Vuitton collarless jacket and matching belt. His teammate, Patrick Mahomes, rocked Adidas from head to toe with Oakley sunglasses.

Here are the top fits ahead of "Sunday Night Football."

Sunday afternoon arrivals

Dallas Cowboys wide receiver George Pickens kept it simple up top, with a pop of color below for his arrival ahead of a divisional game against the Washington Commanders on Sunday. Pickens wore a solid black T-shirt, multicolored striped shorts, and purple-and-black Nike Dunks on the feet.

Commanders' rookie linebacker Sonny Styles was among the best dressed players during the arrivals for the Sunday afternoon games. Styles arrived in a grey suit, with his initials embroidered on the collar in gold.

articles.headline: Fantasy football buzz: Six replacement options for Puka Nacua on 'Monday Night Football'
articles.description: With Puka Nacua ruled out for the game against the New York Giants on Monday night, here are some potential last-minute replacements.
articles.headlineJa: ファンタジーフットボール情報：「マンデーナイトフットボール」でプカ・ナクアの代役となる6つの候補
articles.descriptionJa: 月曜夜のニューヨーク・ジャイアンツ戦でプカ・ナクアの欠場が決まったため、直前で代役となり得る選手をご紹介します。
articles.body:
Everything that happens in the NFL has additional context when viewed from a fantasy football perspective. From position battles to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values in fantasy football.

Our fantasy football buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers and our NFL Nation reporters, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around the league.

Sept. 21: Nacua ruled out for 'Monday Night Football'

By Michael F. Florio

Rams superstar wide receiver Puka Nacua has been ruled out for "Monday Night Football" because of a hip injury. That leaves Davante Adams as the top target for Matthew Stafford against the New York Giants.

For those fantasy managers who rolled the dice on Nacua's availability, replacement options are Malachi Fields, Tutu Atwell, Konata Mumpfield and Darnell Mooney. For those who left him in the flex spot, Terrance Ferguson is an upside option whom I would use over all those receivers except Fields. If you have Blake Corum available to plug in as your flex, he is the top option.

Sept. 21: Kyler Murray clears protocol, will start Week 3

By Michael F. Florio

Kyler Murray has cleared the concussion protocol and will start in Week 3 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. We have not seen much of Murray in a Vikings uniform, but he brings QB1 upside due to his rushing ability and the matchup.

The Bucs have allowed 234 passing yards per game, which ranks 11th highest in the NFL. That is after allowing the sixth-most passing yards in the NFL in 2025. Last week they allowed 19.72 fantasy points to Deshaun Watson, 11th-best among QBs through Sunday.

Murray was a fantasy target of mine this summer due to him being in the best system of his career, with great pass catchers around him. He has been top 12 in fantasy points per game among QBs in every year but one of his career. That is largely due to his rushing ability and highlights the safe floor he brings.

Some QBs I would start him over in Week 3 are Drake Maye, Matthew Stafford, Baker Mayfield and Jordan Love.

Which Commanders should you start with Daniels out?

Marcus Mariota is expected to start Week 3 for the Washington Commanders as Jayden Daniels continues to seek opinions on his dislocated left elbow. Daniels does not have a timetable as of now.

Mariota started eight games for the Commanders last season, averaging 200 passing yards and 32 rushing yards per game. He threw 10 touchdowns and added another with his legs.

Mariota is not someone fantasy managers should be looking to force into their lineups. He is more an option for those in superflex leagues who now find themselves in a pinch. He brings a safer floor than you might expect, thanks to the rushing numbers, but falls far short of Daniels' ceiling.

articles.headline: Seahawks plan to have Sam Darnold back at practice Wednesday
articles.description: Coach Mike Macdonald also said "there is a chance" that quarterback Sam Darnold will play this week at Washington.
articles.headlineJa: シーホークス、サム・ダーノルドが水曜日の練習に復帰する計画
articles.descriptionJa: マイク・マクドナルドHCは、QBサム・ダーノルドが今週のワシントン戦に出場する「可能性がある」とも語りました。
articles.body:
SCOTTSDALE, Ariz. -- Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold is set to return to practice Wednesday after missing most of the team's first two games because of a glute injury, coach Mike Macdonald said Monday.

"Right now, the plan is for him to be out there in some capacity, and we'll go from there," Macdonald said. "How much, we'll see from here to Wednesday on what that number is. But right now, that's the goal."

Earlier Monday, on his Seattle Sports 710-AM radio show, Macdonald said "there is a chance" that Darnold will play this week against the Washington Commanders at Northwest Stadium.

Darnold went down on the fifth play of the Seahawks' Sept. 9 opener and did not practice last week. After the Seahawks improved to 2-0 with a 31-7 win Sunday over the Arizona Cardinals, Macdonald said Darnold is ahead of schedule and that his timetable for returning has "shifted quite drastically" for the better.

Since replacing Darnold, backup Drew Lock has completed nearly 73% of his passes while throwing four touchdown passes with zero turnovers. Lock's Total QBR of 86.4 is fourth best among all quarterbacks through two weeks.

Asked about Lock's play, Macdonald indicated that it won't factor into the team's decision on whether Darnold starts Sunday, saying, "If Sam can play, he's going to play."

In other Seahawks injury news, Macdonald said rookie running back Jadarian Price's shoulder injury does not appear to be serious. The team's first-round pick left late in the third quarter Sunday and did not return.

"It's something we'll monitor throughout the week," Macdonald said. "Shouldn't be a long-term thing."

Price started each of the first two games while Zach Charbonnet -- Seattle's co-starter last season -- continues to work his way back from February ACL surgery. Charbonnet has to miss at least the next two games while on the physically unable to perform list, but a new PUP rule this year would allow the Seahawks to open his 21-day practice window Wednesday. Macdonald said they are still working through that possibility.
